svg.title: Erdős #243, the last step of the cubic-rate proof. Above, two records of successive tails reduced modulo 7: numerators 1, 6, 0, 2 under the rule 2n(n+1)(n+2) + 1, and 4, 5, 0, 1 under 2n(n+1)(n+2) - 1. Beneath the zero the denominator is 5 or 6; the denominator d just before the zero is ringed in red. A bracket over the next two updates reads d squared = 2; a bracket over the preceding update reads d + 2 = (d0 + 3) squared, or 2 (d0 - 1) squared. Below, the seven residues are the candidates for d, each with an arrow to its square: arrows land only on the hatched 0, 1, 2 and 4, and the two red arrows into 2 come from 3 and 4. Under each candidate stands d + 2, hatched when it is a square; the red +2 arrows from 3 and 4 land on 5 and 6, which are not squares, so no denominator serves both sides.
